regional_status: Prevalent across Punjab and Haryana plains during warm, humid spells of October-December.
symptoms: Initial symptoms appear on older lower leaves as small, dark brown to black circular or angular spots with characteristic concentric rings creating a 'target board' effect. Lesions may enlarge, coalesce, and cause premature defoliation.
favorable_conditions: Alternating dry and warm periods with high relative humidity (above 80%) and temperatures between 24°C to 29°C.
prevention_practices: Use certified disease-free seed tubers from verified Punjab/Haryana seed growers.
Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops for at least 2-3 years.
Ensure balanced fertilization; avoid excessive nitrogen which delays leaf maturity.
Maintain adequate spacing to promote airflow within the canopy and reduce leaf wetness.
management_practices: Destroy and burn infected crop debris and volunteer plants post-harvest.
Apply protective contact fungicides such as Mancozeb 75 WP or Chlorothalonil 75 WP at first sign of lower leaf spotting.
In severe outbreaks under humid conditions, consult PAU/HAU spray schedule for systemic fungicides (e.g., Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole).
Follow safe waiting periods (PHI) before tuber harvesting.
safety_warning: Always wear protective gloves and face masks when handling fungicides. Spray during calm morning or evening hours. Adhere strictly to the CIB&RC approved label instructions.

regional_status: Major destructive disease in Punjab and Haryana during foggy, overcast winter months (December-January).
symptoms: Water-soaked, irregular pale to dark green lesions near leaf margins and tips. Under cool, humid conditions, lesions expand rapidly into large brown-black dead areas with delicate white cottony fungal growth on the underside of leaves. Infected tubers show irregular purplish-brown dry rot.
favorable_conditions: Temperatures between 10°C to 20°C with persistent high relative humidity (>90%) and morning fogs or dew.
prevention_practices: Select resistant or tolerant varieties recommended by PAU/CPRI (e.g., Kufri Pukhraj, Kufri Jyoti).
Treat seed tubers with approved protective fungicide before planting.
Avoid excess furrow irrigation that maintains standing water or excessive humidity in fields.
Regularly scout fields when PAU/HAU issues late blight weather warnings.
management_practices: Apply preventive protective spray of Mancozeb 75 WP as soon as weather conditions become favorable for blight.
If disease appears, switch to systemic fungicides such as Cymoxanil + Mancozeb or Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb as recommended by local KVK.
Halt irrigation immediately upon noticing blight spread.
De-haulm (cut and destroy haulms) 10-15 days before harvest to prevent tuber infection from dying leaves.
safety_warning: Wear protective gear during chemical spraying. Ensure proper disposal of chemical containers. Do not feed infected foliage to livestock.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves, uniform canopy, absence of necrotic lesions, concentric rings, chlorosis, or wilting.
favorable_conditions: Well-drained sandy loam soil, optimal soil moisture, balanced NPK application.
prevention_practices: Maintain timely earthing-up to prevent tuber greening.
Monitor for early aphid populations (Myzus persicae) to prevent viral spread.
Follow balanced potassium application for strong cell walls and disease resilience.
management_practices: Continue standard irrigation scheduling avoiding waterlogging.
Routinely inspect under-canopy foliage for any early micro-symptoms.
safety_warning: Routine field operations require standard farm safety precautions.
